correctness.rationale: The eight sufficient bisectors are derived by coordinatewise nearest-neighbor reduction over the infinite periodic set. Their exact six vertices give area 2, common circumradius squared 1+t^4/4, radial moment (4+2t²-t⁴)/12, and perimeter 2 Phi(t²). The exact inequalities q-second-derivative positive and u times q-first-derivative / q below 1 on [0,1], using 32/(5sqrt5)>9/4, prove Phi-second-derivative positive and a unique positive critical point between opposite endpoint derivative signs. Separate symbolic checks of moments, radii, finite comparison witnesses and radical identity replayed successfully. No computational search is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: At fixed point density and equal cell area, total Voronoi interface per area, covering radius and average squared nearest-site distance represent natural distinct geometric quality measures. The theorem completely classifies the unique non-Bravais perimeter optimum of a minimal two-coset periodic grid and proves rigorously that pursuing it worsens both nearest-site objectives. The 0.134% numerical improvement is small and not touted as an engineering gain; the value is the sharp geometric incompatibility and unique symmetry-breaking transition.
